questions.prompt: Under the UK Data Protection Act 2018, which is a legal right of data subjects?
options: To have inaccurate personal data corrected
To demand a copy of the organisation's source code
To prevent any automated processing of any kind
To access any other individual's data on request
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the right to rectification of inaccurate personal data is a core GDPR/DPA right.
questions.feedbackWrong: Data subject rights cover access, rectification, erasure and objection for their own data — not others' data or the organisation's intellectual property.

mistakes.correction: Subjects can object to certain automated decisions with significant effect — not all automated processing, which is ubiquitous and lawful with a valid basis.

questions.prompt: State the three offences defined by the Computer Misuse Act 1990 and give a one-line example of each.

markScheme.text: Unauthorised access to computer material — e.g. guessing someone's password and reading their files.
Unauthorised access with intent to commit further offences — e.g. accessing a system in order to commit fraud.
Unauthorised modification of computer material — e.g. planting malware or deleting/altering data.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a local and a global variable?
options: A local variable exists only within the subroutine or block where it is declared
A local variable can be used anywhere in the program
A global variable is destroyed after each subroutine call
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — local variables are scoped to their declaring subroutine/block and invisible outside it.
questions.feedbackWrong: Scope: locals live inside their declaring subroutine or block only; globals are visible program-wide and persist.

mistakes.correction: It's the local that dies when its subroutine returns — the global persists for the program's lifetime.

questions.prompt:
This recursive function computes triangular numbers:
```
function tri(n)
  if n == 1 then return 1
  return n + tri(n - 1)
endfunction
```
Enter the value returned by tri(5).

mistakes.misconception: Stops the recursion one level early — misses the base-case term.
mistakes.correction: The base case n=1 returns 1, which must be added: the sum is 5+4+3+2+1, all five terms.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between black-box and white-box testing, and state one situation where each is the more appropriate choice.

markScheme.text: Black-box: tests inputs/outputs against the specification without knowledge of internal code.
White-box: tests designed with knowledge of the code structure, aiming to cover paths/branches.
Black-box appropriate: acceptance testing by users or independent testers verifying requirements.
White-box appropriate: unit testing during development to exercise edge paths in the logic.

options: Iterative cycles with working software delivered frequently and requirements revisited
All requirements fixed and documented before any coding begins
Testing happens only after the entire system is built
A single sequential pass through analysis, design, build, test
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — agile delivers working increments in short iterations and embraces changing requirements.
questions.feedbackWrong: Agile is iterative and incremental: frequent working releases, continuous feedback, evolving requirements — the opposite of waterfall's fixed sequential phases.

mistakes.correction: Single sequential passes are the waterfall model — agile deliberately repeats small cycles instead.

questions.prompt: List three input validation checks a program should apply when accepting a user's age in years, and state what each prevents.

markScheme.text: Type check — rejects non-numeric input that would crash arithmetic.
Range check — rejects impossible values (negative, or above ~120).
Presence/length check — rejects empty input before further processing.

questions.prompt: The key obligation the GPL open-source licence imposes on redistributors is:
options: Derivative works must also be distributed under the GPL with source available
The software may never be sold
All derivative works must credit the original author in the program title
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — copyleft: GPL derivatives must stay GPL-licensed with source code available.
questions.feedbackWrong: GPL's copyleft requires derivatives to carry the same licence and offer source — commercial use and sale are explicitly permitted.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses open source with non-commercial restrictions.
mistakes.correction: Open source licences cannot prohibit commercial use — that would violate the Open Source Definition. GPL restricts licensing, not commerce.
